The facade installation process for a metal cladding project in India has nine stages: site survey, anchor and sub-frame layout, waterproofing check, panel delivery and labelling, panel fixing, joints and sealing, alignment checks, cleaning, and handover with documents. For a typical 1,000 to 2,500 sq ft residential project, Metaguise plans about 2 to 3 weeks for on-site installation, after 1 to 2 weeks of design and 4 to 6 weeks of fabrication.
Key takeaways

• Installation is where a good design either holds or fails. Panels that are perfect in the factory can look wrong if the sub-frame is out of line. • The sub-frame matters more than the visible panel. It carries wind load and absorbs thermal movement. • Every panel should arrive numbered, so it goes on the wall in the planned sequence. • A written handover, with drawings, finish details and care instructions, is part of the job.
Why installation decides how a facade looks in year five

Most owners judge a facade by the panel they see. Installers and engineers judge it by what sits behind the panel: the anchors, the sub-frame, the drainage path and the joints. A facade can pass the day-one photograph and still show waves, open joints or water stains after two monsoons if these hidden parts were rushed.

Metaguise designs, fabricates and installs with its own teams, so the drawings, the factory and the site work from one model. That is the main reason we describe installation as a stage of engineering, not a stage of labour. If you want to see the earlier stages, read how facade panels are manufactured in India.
Step 1: Site survey and as-built measurement
Drawings show how a building was meant to be built. The survey shows how it was actually built. Walls are rarely perfectly plumb, slab edges vary, and openings drift from the plan.

A proper survey records wall flatness, slab edge positions, window and door openings, existing services, and access for equipment. These measurements feed the shop drawings, so panel sizes and sub-frame brackets are adjusted before anything is cut. Skipping this step is the most common reason for panels that do not line up at corners.
Step 2: Anchor layout and sub-frame

The sub-frame is the hidden framework, usually aluminium or steel, that the cladding mounts on. It transfers wind pressure and panel weight back to the structural wall. Our article on how metal facade engineering works explains the load path in more detail.
On site, the work runs in this order:

1. Mark anchor points from the approved drawings. 2. Fix brackets to the structure, using the anchor type the engineer specified for that wall material. 3. Install vertical and horizontal rails, with bracket systems that allow adjustment for plumb variation. 4. Check line and level across the full elevation before any panel goes up.
Brackets should allow the metal to expand and contract. A rigid sub-frame with no movement allowance is a fatigue problem waiting to happen.
Step 3: Waterproofing and insulation check

If the wall has a waterproofing layer or insulation, it must be finished and inspected before cladding covers it. In perforated, mesh or ventilated systems the visible panel is not the main weather barrier, so the layer behind it does the weatherproofing. Our guide to what is hiding behind the panel you see covers each layer.
Step 4: Panel delivery, labelling and storage

Panels should arrive packed to avoid scratches and dents, and each one should carry a number that matches the installation drawing. On large jobs, panels are packed in installation sequence, so the crew does not hunt through crates at height. Store panels flat or on edge as advised, off the ground, away from cement dust and wet areas, with the protective film left on until the panel is fixed.
Step 5: Fixing the panels

Panels are fixed section by section, starting from the agreed reference line. Typical practice for flat systems such as SolidPanel is concealed mechanical fixing at the panel edges into a precision aluminium sub-frame, so no fixing heads show on the face.
Fixing details for fins and louvers. Vertical and horizontal fins are usually fixed to brackets or tubes on the sub-frame. Good aluminium fins fixing details share a few points:

• A consistent setback from the wall, so the fin line stays straight. • Slotted or floating connections where length is large, so thermal movement does not twist the fin. • Fixings of compatible metal, to avoid corrosion where two metals touch. • Clear access for future inspection.
The exact detail depends on fin size, spacing and wind exposure, so it must come from the engineer, not from a standard sketch. See how fins behave visually in our guide to architectural fins design.
Step 6: Joints, sealants and drainage

Joints do two jobs. They hide small tolerances and they let panels move. A hairline shadow gap, such as the 10 mm standard gap on SolidPanel, looks crisp only if the sub-frame behind it is accurate. Sealants should be checked at perimeters, and drainage channels and weep holes must stay clear so water can leave the cavity.
Step 7: Alignment and quality checks

At each section, the team checks panel flatness, joint width, line and level, finish consistency and fixing completeness. Colour consistency is checked across batches, which matters on large elevations. On the Miraj Stadium project, thousands of repeated modules had to read as one gold tone, which is why batch tracking and sequence packing were planned from the start. Read more in the Miraj Stadium facade story.
Step 8: Cleaning and handover

Before handover, panels are cleaned of site dust, protective film is removed, and the team walks the elevation with the client or architect. Handover should include as-built drawings, finish and colour references, the written warranty, and a care plan. Our metal facade maintenance guide lists cleaning schedules by climate.
How long does installation take?

For a standard residential project of 1,000 to 2,500 sq ft, Metaguise plans about 8 to 12 weeks end to end: 1 to 2 weeks of design, 4 to 6 weeks of fabrication and 2 to 3 weeks of installation. Special finishes can add 1 to 2 weeks. Large or complex buildings take longer, and monsoon, access equipment and approvals all affect the date.

Frequently asked questions

1. What is the facade installation process?

It is the on-site sequence of survey, sub-frame, waterproofing check, panel fixing, sealing, alignment checks and handover that turns fabricated panels into a finished facade.

2. Who installs a metal facade in India?

Either the facade company’s own team or a subcontractor. Metaguise uses in-house teams so design, fabrication and installation stay coordinated.

3. How long does facade installation take?

About 2 to 3 weeks on site for a standard 1,000 to 2,500 sq ft residential project, after design and fabrication. Larger buildings take longer.

4. Can a facade be installed on an existing building?

Yes. Recladding is common, and a survey of the existing wall decides the sub-frame design. See our guide on retrofit facades.

5. How are fins fixed to a facade?

Usually to brackets on a sub-frame, with slotted connections for movement and compatible metals to prevent corrosion. The exact detail must be engineered for the project.

6. Can installation continue in the monsoon?

Work at height depends on safety and weather. Plan the schedule with a buffer, and protect stored panels from moisture.
